title: Washington picked this very Thursday, November 26

scenes.narration: Today, Thursday, November 26, the United States celebrates Thanksgiving. And 237 years ago, George Washington picked the exact same date: Thursday, November 26.

U.S. National Archives (NARA) vía Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:George_Washington%27s_October_3,_1789,_Thanksgiving_Day_Proclamation._-_NARA_-_299956.jpg

scenes.narration: On September 28, 1789, just before leaving for recess, the first Congress asked the President to recommend a day of thanksgiving. The reason: they had peacefully established a new government.
scenes.image_credit: Federal Hall, N.Y. 1789 ppmsca.15703. Amos Doolittle, Public domain. Library of Congress vía Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Federal_Hall,_N.Y._1789_ppmsca.15703.jpg

scenes.narration: On October 3, in New York, Washington signed the proclamation: I do recommend and assign Thursday the 26th day of November next. It was the first Thanksgiving under the new Constitution.
scenes.image_credit: Gilbert Stuart - George Washington - Google Art Project. Gilbert Stuart, Public domain. Google Arts & Culture vía Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Gilbert_Stuart_-_George_Washington_-_Google_Art_Project.jpg

scenes.narration: And how did he spend it? He went to St. Paul's Chapel, but wrote in his diary that the day was so stormy that few people came. And he gave seven pounds, ten shillings and four pence for food and beer for prisoners jailed for debt.
scenes.image_credit: St. Paul's Chapel - NYC (51522449420). ajay_suresh, CC BY 2.0. Wikimedia Commons: https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:St._Paul%27s_Chapel_-_NYC_(51522449420).jpg

capa.etiqueta: food and beer for debtors in jail

scenes.narration: But it didn't become a fixed holiday. Lincoln set it on the last Thursday of November in 1863. In 1939, Roosevelt moved it a week earlier to stretch Christmas shopping, and there were two Thanksgivings. In 1941, Congress fixed it on the fourth Thursday.

scenes.narration: That's why today matches 1789: same month, same day, same day of the week. The last time was in 2020. So, what are you thankful for?
